newsitem.title: CHINA: China says army contributes to Tibet development.
newsitem.headline: China says army contributes to Tibet development.

text.p: China's garrison in Tibet has made a major contribution to development in the remote Himalayan region and acted as a steel Great Wall defending national unity, the People's Daily Overseas Edition said on Wednesday.

Tibetans recognised that Chinese troops stationed in the remote and backward region had brought social and economic progress while protecting stability and national unity, it quoted Gyaincain Norbu, chairman of the Tibet Autonomous Region, as saying.

"If there was no people's army...Tibetan people would not have their current happiness and even more beautiful future," Norbu said at a meeting in Lhasa on Monday to mark the 70th anniversary of the founding of the People's Liberation Army.
"The People's Liberation Army and Armed Police in Tibet are a steel Great Wall protecting the unity of the motherland and Tibet's stability," he said.
Troops in Tibet have built more than 200 roads, 150 power stations and four airports in the region, he said.
China has maintained a large military presence in the restive region since its troops marched into Tibet in 1950.

China has regularly used paramilitary police to crush unrest by pro-independence activists while Beijing maintains a huge army presence in Tibet both to control the local population and to protect its border with India.
